prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Offshore wind O&M; scope: offshore assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel, external orgs, electrical up to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere: boundary, dispatch, authorized signals, supply/protection status); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): executes authorized control, limits output, blocks protection-conflicting commands, reports state, safe mode on auxiliary loss; produces Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet (interlocks), Nacelle Condition Monitor; Turbine Sensor Bus collects their measurements. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur): produces Leading Edge Tile Image in close-range survey; shall repeat pass if coverage insufficient. Blade Specialist reviews evidence, reports if more examination needed. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers; sends Transformer Tap Snapshot on request. Substation Operator confirms constraints, applies authorized switching, records state. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, V/f limits, no unapproved paralleling, sheds nonessential, failure→alarm. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): time-stamped observations/alarms to Shore Control Room (Amber Quay); flags work from Pitch Deviation Notice; produces Session Revocation Receipt. Shore Control Room escalates hazards; retains decision record, observations, outcome. Control Engineer: validates data (stale→unverified, not sole basis for intrusive task), records basis, requests inspection, reassesses after findings/corrected data; findings compared to observations before closure. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): ranks work using Squall Window Bulletin; produces Deferred Task Rationale. Duty Planner: selects mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck), Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master; submits task scope/location/crew/window for permit. Crew Transfer Vessel uses Harness Audit Card before transfer. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard) uses Position Quality Flag. Grid Dispatcher: alarms safety>protection>export. Marine Coordinator; Vessel Master accepts/pauses/aborts. Weather Analyst uses Wave Burst Record. Port Agent issues Berth Slot Confirmation. Permits: authorization ≠ proof of safe state. Redoubt (permit control) shall block release until risk reviews/isolation references complete. HSE Officer confirms controls. Field Supervisor validates method/party, starts work only when permit active and isolations independently verified, briefs crew. Electrical Technician identifies isolations, secures turbine, live-dead-live test;

Document units:
S333: A change in equipment condition, task scope, or operating constraint requires the Field Supervisor to pause work and reassess the authorization.
S334: The Duty Planner coordinates any revised work window with the relevant operational roles before the permit is amended.
S335: The Field Supervisor confirms that tools, temporary connections, and personnel are clear before requesting isolation removal.
S336: The Electrical Technician checks that the work area is ready for restoration and reports any outstanding defects or restrictions.
S337: The Substation Operator removes isolations only under the approved switching process and records each restoration action.
S338: The Control Engineer reviews the restored equipment state and confirms that required operational checks are complete.
S339: The Shore Control Room retains the permit status, isolation history, test results, and restoration decision for operational review.
S340: The Duty Planner closes the work authorization after the Field Supervisor confirms completion or formally records any remaining work.
S341: Equipment returns to service only when operating personnel accept the restored condition and any applicable restrictions are communicated.
S342: The Substation Operator maintains the Offshore Substation within approved operating limits and follows current switching instructions.
S343: At the start of each shift, the operator reviews alarms, active restrictions, equipment status, and handover notes.
S344: Routine rounds cover room temperature, ventilation, water ingress, lighting, access control, and visible signs of damage.
S345: The operator checks Main Transformer temperatures, cooling equipment, oil indications, and abnormal noise against established limits.
S346: The Export Cable Monitor is reviewed for trends or alarms that require escalation to the Control Engineer.
S347: The Grid Interface Relay is checked for healthy indications and consistency with the approved grid operating state.
S348: The SCADA Gateway displays are compared with local indications when equipment status is uncertain.
S349: The Control Engineer investigates unexplained discrepancies before operating personnel rely on remote indications.
S350: The Work Permit Portal is checked to confirm that active work authorizations and isolation boundaries remain current.
S351: The operator verifies that personnel access records are consistent with the planned work and current site occupancy.
S352: The Fire Detection Panel is checked for healthy status, active faults, and unobstructed access to response equipment.
S353: The Emergency Generator produces the Start Test Trace during its scheduled functional test.
S354: The operator confirms fuel level, starting battery condition, ventilation, and readiness of the Emergency Generator for loss of normal supply.
